summary: Verified mobile pinch-zoom and ILLUSTRATION label regression against the PRODUCTION yarn build (main.28b6e8b0.js) served via the preview-origin fixture at /__production_check__/*.txt. Ran WebKit iPhone + Chromium mobile (390x844) + Chromium desktop (1920x800). All 7 destination labels mount in production in both engines. Pinch spread zooms in to FOV45 (clamped) and pinch-in restores the widest-framing starting view exactly. Footer 'A CREATIVE WORLD' present.
verified_items: ILLUSTRATION label mounts in production bundle on WebKit iPhone 390x844: data-testid=destination-label-illustration present with text 'ILLUSTRATION', display:block, visible in viewport (rect x=25.4 y=321.8 w=100 h=16.5). Same for Chromium mobile UA. Previous regression (iteration_3) is FIXED by the native DOM DestinationLabel in Destination.jsx replacing drei <Html> which had a React 19 production inner-root race.
All 7 labels (illustration, murals, packaging, printing, fashion, games, contact) mount in both WebKit mobile, Chromium mobile and Chromium desktop production bundle (none missing).

Mobile pinch-zoom via CDP two-touch gestures demonstrably changes projected label coordinates: illustration label cx=75.4 at initial widest framing → cx=-283 after 2-finger spread (zoom-in) → cx=-322.7 after additional spreads (clamp at FOV=45) → cx=75.4 (exact initial value) after pinch-in. This proves both limits of CameraRig: upper clamp at FOV=45 and lower clamp at farFraming=max(1,2/aspect). zoom.current ref correctly persists between gestures and clamps consistently.
Single-finger drag on canvas did not alter framing (no stray zoom from one-touch).

Chromium desktop 1920x800 production build: all labels mount, footer 'A CREATIVE WORLD' present, and because CameraRig returns early when farFraming===1, no touch listeners attach on desktop (desktop still uses FOV45).
Footer 'A CREATIVE WORLD' confirmed in page text on desktop production build.
critical_code_review_comments: CameraRig.jsx: pinch state resets to null on any touch count change but does not re-arm when the user adds a second finger mid-drag. A user who starts a 1-finger pan and then adds a second finger will not pinch-zoom until all fingers are released and both re-pressed. Minor UX; current implementation matches typical native behavior.

CameraRig.jsx useEffect dep list includes size.width/size.height; on orientation change the effect reruns with a fresh zoom.current snapshot of framing - verified bounds are kept but mid-gesture pinch state is lost on orientation flip (acceptable).

Destination.jsx DestinationLabel appends a plain DOM element to gl.domElement.parentNode. Depends on canvas parent being stable; works for current World.jsx layout. Consider using the canvas container ref instead of parentNode to be robust to future wrapper changes.

Minor: DestinationLabel scale formula uses camera.fov so labels will shrink/enlarge with zoom on desktop; on mobile scale is hard-coded to 1 (labels do not grow when zoomed in). Intentional per code but worth confirming with the designer that mobile labels are expected to not scale with FOV.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable: /app/test_reports/pw_prod_zoom_test.py routes the preview origin to the production yarn build via fixture TXTs. Uses Chromium (/pw-browsers/chromium-1248/chrome-linux-arm64/chrome) and WebKit (/pw-browsers/webkit-2370). CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent is used for 2-finger pinch gestures. Note: direct r3f camera.fov readback via fiber tree returned null (production minification obscures hooks); verification instead uses projected label screen coords as the FOV proxy. Main agent must remove the temporary /__production_check__/*.txt fixtures after this iteration.
rca of the issue: Previous iteration_3 regression (ILLUSTRATION missing in production) was caused by drei <Html> inner React root mount race on first-size flip under React 19 production scheduler. Current fix in Destination.jsx replaces always-visible <Html> label with a direct DOM element appended once in useLayoutEffect and positioned per-frame via camera.project. Verified: no mount race in production WebKit or Chromium mobile.
